title: The Seven Summits — Highest Peaks on Each of the 7 Continents
answer: The Seven Summits are the highest mountain peaks on each of Earth's seven continents: Asia (Mount Everest, 8,848.86 m), South America (Aconcagua, 6,961 m), North America (Denali, 6,190 m), Africa (Mount Kilimanjaro, 5,895 m), Europe (Mount Elbrus, 5,642 m), Antarctica (Vinson Massif, 4,892 m), and Australasia/Oceania (Puncak Jaya, 4,884 m / Mount Kosciuszko, 2,228 m).

title: The World's Longest Rivers (Nile, Amazon, Yangtze, Mississippi)
answer: The longest river in the world is the Nile River in Africa at approximately 6,650 km (4,132 mi), followed by the Amazon River in South America (~6,400 km, largest by discharge volume), the Yangtze River in China (6,300 km, longest in Asia), and the Mississippi-Missouri river system in North America (6,275 km).
highlights: 1. Nile River: ~6,650 km (4,132 miles) — Africa (Mediterranean Sea basin)
2. Amazon River: ~6,400 km (3,977 miles) — South America (Discharges ~209,000 m³/s, 20% of global river discharge)
3. Yangtze River (Chang Jiang): 6,300 km (3,917 miles) — China (Site of the Three Gorges Dam)
4. Mississippi-Missouri River: 6,275 km (3,902 miles) — United States (Gulf of Mexico basin)
5. Yenisei River: 5,539 km (3,442 miles) — Russia/Mongolia (Arctic Ocean basin)
6. Yellow River (Huang He): 5,464 km (3,395 miles) — China ('Cradle of Chinese Civilization')
7. Congo River: 4,700 km (2,920 miles) — Africa (Deepest river in the world, exceeding 220 m depth)

title: Major World Lakes: Caspian Sea, Lake Superior & Lake Baikal
answer: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest enclosed inland water body by both area (371,000 km²) and volume. Lake Superior in North America is the world's largest freshwater lake by surface area (82,100 km²), while Lake Baikal in Siberia (Russia) is the world's deepest lake (1,642 m) and largest freshwater lake by volume (holding 20% of the world's unfrozen surface freshwater).
highlights: Caspian Sea (371,000 km²): World's largest lake / inland sea (endorheic saline basin bounded by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan)
Lake Superior (82,100 km²): Largest freshwater lake by surface area (USA/Canada Great Lakes system)
Lake Victoria (68,870 km²): Africa's largest lake by area, shared by Uganda, Kenya, and Tanzania; chief reservoir of the White Nile
Lake Baikal (1,642 m depth / 23,615 km³ volume): Deepest and oldest (~25 million years) freshwater lake on Earth; contains more water than all North American Great Lakes combined
Dead Sea: Hypersaline lake between Israel and Jordan; lowest land elevation on Earth (-430.5 m below sea level)

title: The World's Major Deserts (Sahara, Gobi, Atacama, Thar)
answer: The largest desert on Earth is the Antarctic Polar Desert (14.2 million km²), followed by the Arctic Polar Desert (13.9 million km²). The largest subtropical hot desert is the Sahara Desert in Northern Africa (9.2 million km²). The Atacama Desert in Chile is the driest non-polar desert in the world.
highlights: Polar Deserts: Antarctic Desert (14.2M km²) & Arctic Desert (13.9M km²)
Sahara Desert: 9.2 million km² across 11 North African nations; largest hot desert
Gobi Desert: 1.3 million km² cold winter desert spanning northern China and southern Mongolia
Kalahari Desert: 900,000 km² semi-arid sandy savannah in Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa
Atacama Desert: Driest non-polar desert on Earth, located in northern Chile between the Andes and the Pacific Ocean (some weather stations have recorded zero rainfall for centuries)
Thar Desert (Great Indian Desert): ~200,000 km² arid region spanning northwestern India (Rajasthan, Gujarat) and eastern Pakistan

title: Major Strategic Maritime Straits & Trade Chokepoints
answer: Strategic straits are narrow sea corridors vital for global shipping and energy trade: the Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman (transiting ~20% of global petroleum); the Strait of Malacca connects the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea; and the Strait of Gibraltar connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea.
highlights: Strait of Hormuz: Between Iran and Oman/UAE; world's most critical crude oil transit chokepoint
Strait of Malacca: Between Sumatra (Indonesia) and the Malay Peninsula; shortest sea route between Indian and Pacific Oceans (handles ~25% of global traded goods and 60% of China's oil imports)
Strait of Gibraltar: Between Spain (Europe) and Morocco (Africa); 14 km (8.9 mi) wide waterway connecting the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea
Bab-el-Mandeb (Gate of Tears): Connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden / Arabian Sea; critical corridor for ships transiting the Suez Canal
Bosphorus & Dardanelles: Turkish straits connecting the Black Sea to the Mediterranean Sea, dividing Istanbul between Europe and Asia
Bering Strait: 82 km wide strait separating Cape Dezhnev (Russia / Asia) from Cape Prince of Wales (Alaska / North America)

title: Important Himalayan Mountain Passes of India
answer: Himalayan mountain passes are strategic high-altitude corridors connecting India to neighboring regions: Nathu La (Sikkim – Tibet, historical Silk Road), Shipki La (Himachal Pradesh – Tibet, Sutlej river entry), Rohtang Pass (Himachal Pradesh, Kullu to Lahaul-Spiti), and Zoji La (connects Srinagar to Leh, Ladakh).
highlights: Nathu La Pass: Elevation 4,310 m (14,140 ft) in Sikkim on the Indo-China border; historical branch of the ancient Silk Route
Rohtang Pass: Elevation 3,978 m in Pir Panjal range (Himachal Pradesh); bypassed year-round by the 9.02 km Atal Tunnel at 3,000+ m altitude
Zoji La Pass: Elevation 3,528 m in Greater Himalayas; strategic link connecting Kashmir Valley to Ladakh
Shipki La: Elevation 3,930 m in Kinnaur district, Himachal Pradesh; entry gorge of the Sutlej River from Tibet into India
Lipulekh Pass: Elevation 5,200 m in Uttarakhand at India-Nepal-China trijunction; route for Kailash Mansarovar Yatra
Bomdi La: Elevation 2,217 m in Arunachal Pradesh connecting Tezpur to Tawang and Tibet

title: Mariana Trench — Deepest Point on Earth
answer: The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific Ocean is the deepest oceanic trench on Earth. Its deepest point, Challenger Deep, reaches approximately 10,994 metres (~36,070 feet or nearly 11 km) below sea level. Water pressure at the bottom exceeds 1,086 bar (over 1,000 times standard atmospheric pressure).
